findings.claim: On hydration T10 renders a different state from its server markup until the preset file arrives. On B3 the 'Shared with the other graph' line wraps one row shorter, and everything after it moves up 24 px and then back down.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.6: 'Tools reserve their box size in the HTML so that hydration does not shift the page'; Cumulative Layout Shift at most 0.1 (360 by 800, processor slowed four times).

At 790 ms the text is restored at 98 px. At 4x the tool-frame goes 2050 -> 2026 -> 2050 px. Two layout shifts of 0.1501 follow. Reading position 300 px above .lines, 4x, KaTeX fonts blocked to isolate this cause: CLS 0.3002 on b5. Without blocking: b5 0.3581, b11 0.3002, b12 0.3002, b7 0.3895. At b7's prediction block, fonts blocked: CLS 0.6669 (two shifts of 0.2889 from this cause plus 0.0891 from P4-RT-07-02). Machine: 4 CPUs, Node 22.22.0, Chromium 141, load 2 to 4.

notes: G4 lab item, M7 composition (traces with Lighthouse's categories, 3 runs, 4x, 360x800). (1) The parse, style and layout of the 803 kB, 37079-px document is one task of 1425 to 1563 ms before FCP (Layout 966 to 1062, UpdateLayoutTree 239 to 279, ParseHTML 106 to 160, scripts about 25 ms). It does not count in TBT, because the render-blocking <link rel=expect href=#lesson-parsed> of Lesson.astro (MERGE P3 stage 3.3, DECISIONS) holds the first paint until the end of the parse; it is why LCP sits at 1.7 to 2.6 s (Lighthouse M7 median 2.322 s, one of five runs at 2.597 s). (2) The first-paint task of 100 to 140 ms (PrePaint 37 to 74, Paint 22 to 26) straddles FCP. (3) The KaTeX font swap brings a relayout of 85 to 137 ms and a repaint of 89 to 99 ms after FCP (finding P4-RT-07-03). (4) The client:idle hydration of b1 (T10, A2 root polytope) is one task of 186 to 239 ms. (5) A commit and hit-test task of 60 to 64 ms follows. Trace TBT is 252 to 338 ms.

G4 lab item, b1 hydration JavaScript (CPU profile at 100 us sampling, source-mapped, 3 runs; the profiler inflates times to 282 to 382 ms). Svelte runtime self time is 51 to 57 percent. Engine self time is 33 to 45 ms (about 12 percent): configure -> rootPolytopeRings -> highestRoot -> classify; countsOf -> wythoffFVector and weylOrder; wythoffFaceTypes -> parabolicOrder; orbitGraph for verticesOnMain. The T10 scene and drawing modules account for 42 to 58 ms inclusive (about 15 percent). Board, Roads and Node take 55 to 89 ms inclusive; the ToolFrame chrome takes 153 to 219 ms inclusive, of which the figure snippet is 99 to 142. GC takes 6 to 8 ms. No single engine call approaches 50 ms.

G4 lab item, what is and is not at load. Only b1 hydrates, and it sits below the first screen (top 1127 px at 360x800); SPEC 7.6 still makes the first tool client:idle. No client:visible island hydrates without scrolling. There is no worker request, no other tool's presets, no names.json, no Predict, no SVG writer and no move-graph module; 17 scripts, 82398 B. The only fetches outside scripts are the T10 manifest and A2-r1.1.json. One piece of work is redundant: verticesOnMain computes the A2 orbit on the main thread just before the data file supplies it (6 vertices, negligible). Counterfactuals (observer TBT, alternated, 5 runs each, load 1.2 to 1.5): as built, median 319 ms (214 to 367); with the three KaTeX fonts preloaded, 199 ms (138 to 263); with the T10 chunk blocked (no hydration), 92 ms (75 to 151). M7 falls under 200 ms only if the font fix is made and b1's hydration task is also shortened, for example by deferring the hidden table view and the controls to a later task. The second step is a decision for the owner.

The engine classifies sub-boards internally: wythoffFaceTypes -> parabolicOrder -> weylOrder(subBoard(...)) classifies every new sub-board object (E-11 caches per object). The result is 7 classify computations on b1's load (A2 once by the tool, 6 sub-boards), 13 on /tools/geometry/ (A3), 35 on picking E8 and 15 on F4. The tool itself calls classify once per board. T10's own timing test and T10.spec.ts's 'no long task on E8 loads' cover the cost.

T10 draws the points twice in the same frame in the vertices-only cases: 34560 arc calls for 17280 points (E8 0.1.0.0.0.0.0.0) and 35840 for 17920 (B7 1.0.0.1.0.0.1). The likely cause is that onVertices and the ready state both draw before the next animation frame. No cap is broken, but drawing up to 20000 points costs twice what it needs.
